correctness.rationale: All 6476 vertex subsets of size at most six fail the exact signature criterion; precisely 268 of 3432 seven-subsets pass. Two separate complete enumerators construct the same Fano incidence graph via cyclic triples and via binary-vector orthogonality, generate all one- and two-replacement edges, and verify the three component sizes (22,224,22), 658 one-replacement edges, exact degrees, component diameters, and the connected at-most-two-replacement graph with 4438 edges and diameter five. The small components have a direct proof as cones on the line graph of the cubic Heawood graph. The all-point to all-line move requires five steps by point-count level changes; the six intermediate codes in RESULT.md witness achievability. Both source programs run from their own complete packages. The theorem has exactly the finite fourteen-vertex domain; no extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The exact Heawood 268-optimal-code roster, its two cone components plus the remaining 224-vertex diameter-six component, and the sharp at-most-two-replacement global connectivity threshold are not implied by the generic Johnson graph relation or by known extremal identifying-code count bounds. Gravier et al. and the full 2015 optimal-code-count paper were inspected; their conclusions address general bounds or extremal multiplicities. The directly relevant 2016 optimal-code ensemble article was only available as abstract and is an explicit residual priority risk, not claimed inspected in full. Searches of published mathematical claims and relevant literature found no exact or dominating Heawood result; absence of a hit is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: The full text of the highly relevant Honkala–Hudry–Lobstein (2016) ensemble paper remained inaccessible; an explicit 14-vertex Heawood worked example there would change originality.
Historical or unindexed computer tables and incidence-code papers could tabulate the same graph.
The status is self-review, not independent confirmation or universal priority proof.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by relocating an optimum set of diagnostically identifying sensors while retaining minimum cardinality at every intermediate state. The proof demonstrates an exact failure of one-sensor mobility: three separated sectors of sizes 22, 224, 22, with interpretable cone-over-line-graph geometry. A two-sensor replacement is sharply necessary and sufficient for global motion, with exact maximum distance five. This is substantive structural information that cannot be inferred from the mere optimal-size count and is a natural complete finite classification, although it makes no broader-family claim.
